newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan vice-president to visit U.S.-paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan vice-president to visit U.S.-paper.

text.p: Washington has agreed to let Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan stop over in two U.S. cities during his trip to Nicaragua in January, a local newspaper in Taiwan reported on Wednesday.

Lien would make a two-day transit stop in New York en route to the inauguration of Nicaraguan President-elect Arnoldo Aleman on January 10, the China Times Express quoted unidentified U.S. officials as saying. Lien would also stop in Los Angeles for one night on his way home from Nicaragua.
China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, strongly objects to Taipei officials visiting countries that have diplomatic ties with Beijing, especially the United States.
Taiwan's presidential office was not available to confirm Lien's U.S. trip because of a national holiday.
Only 30 countries, including Nicaragua, recognise the Republic of China government that retreated to Taiwan in 1949 after losing a civil war to the communists on mainland China.
Beijing held sabre-rattling missile tests near Taiwan after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui made a private, but high-profile, trip to the United States in June 1995.
China recently tightened its diplomatic embargo on Taipei in a long-standing quest to bring Taiwan under Beijing's rule.
It won a major diplomatic victory in November when Taiwan's largest ally, South Africa, announced it would switch recognition to Beijing by the end of 1997.
Taipei has been sending top officials abroad on diplomatic missions in an effort to prevent further desertions.
